top_choice_rationale: P002 (Kiyotaki and Moore) credits one identifiable mechanism with two clear originators: borrowing limits tied to collateral value, together with durable-asset prices, amplify and propagate shocks. The work is about three decades old and has been extended and quantified in the macro-finance literature since 2008. Its mechanism, borrowers' collateral and asset-price feedback, differs from the banks-and-crises work recognised in 2022, and citation wording can keep the two apart. P001 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) has broader influence on research and central-bank practice and is a strong second. Its attribution is contestable because the three-name cap leaves out Galí, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans, Smets and Gertler. As a firm price-setting researcher, I also note that micro evidence treats Calvo-type time-dependent pricing as a convenient approximation, not a description of firm behaviour. I do not treat the ten explicit supporters of P001 as evidence of merit. Both awards rank above no award, because each recognises a mature, original and durable contribution.
recusal_note: No connection to Kiyotaki or Moore (P002) or to Calvo, Taylor or Woodford (P001) is apparent from my profile. Disclosed without adjudication: I co-authored an IJIO 2026 paper on price adjustment with chair John Hassler and former chair Tore Ellingsen, and that topic is thematically close to P001. Hassler supports P001. I am married to Magdalena Andersson, which is a public fact only and has no apparent bearing on any candidate.
